Archstats reads GitHub Actions (.github/workflows), GitLab CI (.gitlab-ci.yml), Jenkinsfiles and Jenkins libraries (vars/*.groovy), Rancher (fleet.yaml, .rancher-pipeline.yml and rancher commands in any pipeline), Azure Pipelines, Bitbucket Pipelines and CircleCI. A workspace that ignores non-source files never reads them.

flags.intro: Each flag is a fact a file states, with the line it is on. Nothing is scored: whether it matters here is your call. Every rule has an assert template in docs/rules/cicd.yml.

base_unpinned_tag.fact: Base image with no tag, or latest
base_unpinned_tag.why: The build changes whenever the image's publisher pushes, with no change here.

base_no_digest.fact: Base image not pinned to a digest
base_no_digest.why: A tag can be moved to other contents; a digest cannot.

runs_as_root.why: Without a USER in the final stage the container runs as the base image's user, root unless it sets one.

add_remote_url.why: The build fetches whatever the URL serves at that moment, unchecked.

secret_like_key.why: ENV and ARG values stay in the image's history, readable by anyone who can pull it. The value is never stored here.

copy_all_no_dockerignore.why: Every file in the build context goes into the image: .git, local env files, build output.

handoff_unpinned.fact: Action, orb, pipe or component not pinned
handoff_unpinned.why: What runs is whatever its owner pushes next, in every pipeline that uses it.

library_unpinned.why: The library changes under every pipeline that loads it.

remote_include_unpinned.fact: Remote include or template not pinned
remote_include_unpinned.why: This pipeline changes when another project's default branch does.

pr_target_checkout_head.fact: pull_request_target checks out the pull request
pr_target_checkout_head.why: It runs a stranger's code with the repository's secrets.

no_permissions_block.why: Its token gets the repository's default, often write access to everything.

curl_pipe_shell.why: It runs whatever the server returns, unchecked.

docker_privileged.why: docker run --privileged gives the container the host.

tls_verify_off.why: Any certificate is accepted, so the connection can be intercepted.

token_literal.fact: Token or password written into a command
token_literal.why: Everyone who can read the repository can read it, and it stays in the history. The value is never stored here.

ungated_prod_deploy.fact: Deploy to production with nothing in front of it
ungated_prod_deploy.why: No manual step, approval or deployment environment stands between a change and production.

push_latest_only.why: Releases cannot be told apart, or rolled back to.
